data.content_ref: inline:The target claims 'safe means read-only (no server state change), while idempotent means state may change but identical repeated requests yield the same result as a single one.' This incorrectly frames safe and idempotent as mutually exclusive concepts defined by the presence or absence of state mutation. According to RFC 9110 §9.2.2, safe methods are themselves idempotent. Idempotency does not require state change; it simply allows for it. The correct distinction is that safe methods are strictly read-only (guaranteed to have no side effects), whereas idempotent methods *may* have side effects but guarantee that repeated identical requests have the same intended effect as a single one. By defining idempotent as intrinsically involving state mutation ('means state may change'), the target provides an inaccurate published definition and fails to precisely distinguish the two properties as requested by the problem.
